title: The chromatophore as an actuator: mechanics, kinetics and a datasheet
headline: Two parameters are fitted to two measured quantities - the sacculus stiffness to the steady-state expansion ratio 2.55, and the dermal damping to the measured expansion:retraction asymmetry, which it reaches (1.27 against 1.34, Renard 2026; Hadjisolomou 2021 puts it at 3.7). The two fits are mutually inconsistent: at that damping the peak expansion collapses to 1.73, 32% short of the ratio the stiffness was fitted to. And the one genuinely free prediction fails: the 90% rise is 232 ms against a measured expansion phase of 67-83 ms, 2.8-3.5x too slow, and the control arm fails. An earlier version of this study claimed a lumped elastic recoil was STRUCTURALLY incapable of retraction slower than expansion; that was wrong, made from a sweep whose maximum sat at its own boundary, and it is corrected here. Across every sweep the stroke is set by the elastic sacculus rather than by the muscle, so adding radial fibres buys almost nothing. Parameters: 5 sourced, 13 assumed, 1 nondimensional.

species_of_evidence.asymmetry_also_scored_against: Euprymna berryi and Sepia officinalis (Renard et al. 2026)
species_of_evidence.muscle_property_proxies_from: Doryteuthis pealeii mantle circular and funnel retractor muscle - a different tissue in the same genus, never a chromatophore radial muscle
species_of_evidence.note: Three animals. This study's fit, its asymmetry comparison and its proxies do not come from one organism, and the page should not read as though they do.

what_changed: comparisons.rise_time_ms is now scored against the expansion PHASE (67-83 ms) rather than the published rise time tRt (117-150 ms), which is timed from the flash and includes a 50-67 ms latency this model does not simulate
comparisons.retraction_vs_expansion_asymmetry now carries BOTH measured sources; it previously carried Renard's 1.338 alone
SUPERSEDED_2026_11_02.superseded_practice: Scoring the asymmetry against Renard's 1.338 alone. Both measured sources are now carried; 1.338 itself remains current.
SUPERSEDED_2026_11_02.effect: The control arm fails by MORE than the earlier version recorded: 2.6-3.2x too slow on rise time instead of 1.4-1.8x, and wrong in sign against two sources instead of one.

model.description: One chromatophore organ: an incompressible neo-Hookean pigment sacculus opened by N Hill-type radial muscle fibres anchored in the dermis and closed by its own stored elastic energy against a dermal dashpot. Inertia is checked and discarded.
equations: F_muscle(r, dr/dt, a) = F_elastic(r) + c dr/dt
F_muscle = N a_fibre sigma_max a fl(r) fv(dr/dt)
da/dt = (u - a)/tau,  tau = tau_act when driving, tau_deact when releasing
pigment disc thickness h(r) = V0 / (pi r^2), volume conserved

parameters.name: r0
parameters.source: Retracted sacculus RADIUS. Bounded by sourced retracted DIAMETERS of 5-100 um (Ukrow J et al. 2025, eLife 106509, PMID 40719173 (read: full text via PMC)) and 15-100 um (Reiter S, Laurent G et al. 2018, Nature 562:361-366, PMID 30333578, read: full text via PMC); no paper we read gives a retracted radius for the species the kinetics were measured in, so the midpoint is assumed.

parameters.name: R_anchor
parameters.source: Dermal anchor radius, i.e. radial fibre reach. Gauld 2021 describes 'an extremely elongated distal end' with no number (Gauld C et al. 2021, J Morphol 282:1081-1093, PMID 33998033 (read: abstract)); 3 x r0 is assumed.

parameters.name: N_muscles
parameters.source: Radial muscle fibres per chromatophore. The literature DISAGREES and all five readings are kept: 10-20 (Ukrow J et al. 2025, eLife 106509, PMID 40719173 (read: full text via PMC) abstract); ~10-15 (same paper's histology methods, Euprymna + Sepia); 15-25 (Renard MDM et al. 2026, eLife 110074, PMID 42418335 (read: full text via PMC)); 19-27 (Kasugai T et al. 2011, PLoS ONE 6:e18244, PMID 21483763 (read: full text via PMC), Sepioteuthis lessoniana); 'several dozen' (Gauld C et al. 2021, J Morphol 282:1081-1093, PMID 33998033 (read: abstract), 3D EM of Doryteuthis pealeii). 20 is the central value and the sweep spans 8-48.

parameters.name: a_fibre
parameters.source: Physiological cross-section of one radial fibre, from an assumed 2 um diameter. Proxy context only: squid funnel retractor fibres are '~3 um across' (Rosenbluth J, Szent-Gyorgyi AG, Thompson JT 2010, J Exp Biol 213:2430-2443, PMID 20581273 (read: abstract) - PROXY: squid funnel retractor, not chromatophore muscle). Nobody we read measured a chromatophore radial fibre's cross-section.

parameters.name: sigma_max
parameters.source: Peak isometric stress. PROXY from other obliquely striated squid muscles: 212 +/- 105 and 290 +/- 166 kN/m2 (Thompson JT, Shelton RM, Kier WM 2014, J Exp Biol 217:2181-2192, PMID 24675565 (read: abstract) - PROXY: squid mantle circular muscle, not chromatophore radial muscle); 270 +/- 20 mN/mm2 (Rosenbluth J, Szent-Gyorgyi AG, Thompson JT 2010, J Exp Biol 213:2430-2443, PMID 20581273 (read: abstract) - PROXY: squid funnel retractor, not chromatophore muscle); 216 and 335 mN/mm2 for CMP and SMR fibres (Thompson JT, Szczepanski JA, Brody J 2008, J Exp Biol 211:1463-1474, PMID 18424680 (read: abstract) - PROXY: squid mantle circular muscle). 250 kPa sits inside all three intervals.

parameters.name: v_max
parameters.source: Unloaded shortening velocity. PROXY: 2.15 +/- 0.26 L0/s (funnel retractor, Rosenbluth J, Szent-Gyorgyi AG, Thompson JT 2010, J Exp Biol 213:2430-2443, PMID 20581273 (read: abstract) - PROXY: squid funnel retractor, not chromatophore muscle); 2.4 (SMR) and 5.1 (CMP) L0/s at 20 C (Thompson JT, Szczepanski JA, Brody J 2008, J Exp Biol 211:1463-1474, PMID 18424680 (read: abstract) - PROXY: squid mantle circular muscle).

parameters.name: hill_curvature
parameters.source: Hill a/P0. Standard value; no cephalopod measurement found.

parameters.name: tau_act
parameters.source: Activation time constant. Bounded by a sourced 8 ms latent period and peak twitch force within 50 ms in squid funnel retractor (Rosenbluth J, Szent-Gyorgyi AG, Thompson JT 2010, J Exp Biol 213:2430-2443, PMID 20581273 (read: abstract) - PROXY: squid funnel retractor, not chromatophore muscle) and by the sourced 50-67 ms whole-organ response latency (Hadjisolomou SP et al. 2021, Front Physiol 12:675252, PMID 34220538 (read: full text via publisher)).

parameters.name: tau_deact
parameters.source: Deactivation time constant; no cephalopod chromatophore measurement found.

parameters.name: L_opt_frac
parameters.source: Optimum fibre length as a fraction of the retracted-state fibre length. Assumed to sit at the retracted state, i.e. the muscle starts on its plateau.

parameters.name: t0_wall
parameters.source: Sacculus wall thickness when retracted. No measurement found; enters only as the product G*t0, which the control arm fits as a single quantity.

parameters.name: G_sacculus
parameters.source: Sacculus shear modulus. THE ONE FITTED PARAMETER: chosen so the steady-state area ratio equals the measured 2.55x (Hadjisolomou SP et al. 2021, Front Physiol 12:675252, PMID 34220538 (read: full text via publisher)). Never measured in any paper we read.

parameters.name: c_damp
parameters.source: Lumped dermal damping at the sacculus rim. Not fitted to the expansion arm; swept, and the value needed to match the measured retraction is reported as a prediction.

parameters.name: eps_max
parameters.source: Maximum fractional shortening the radial fibre can achieve. No measurement found for chromatophore radial muscle; swept over 0.10-0.50.

parameters.name: rho_tissue
parameters.source: Sacculus density, for the inertia check only. Seawater-ish soft tissue.

parameters.name: target_area_ratio
parameters.source: +155.06% mean chromatophore surface-area increase on expansion, so 1 + 1.5506 = 2.5506 (Hadjisolomou SP et al. 2021, Front Physiol 12:675252, PMID 34220538 (read: full text via publisher)). Species: Doryteuthis pealeii. This is the peak of the 4,000 chromatophores that EXPANDED to a startle flash; the paper states no maximum.

parameters.name: target_rise_ms
parameters.source: Expansion PHASE duration tRt - tR per region: 67 ms (head/arms), 67 ms (fin), 83 ms (mantle), computed from Table 1 of Hadjisolomou SP et al. 2021, Front Physiol 12:675252, PMID 34220538 (read: full text via publisher). SUPERSEDES the 117-150 ms used earlier, which was the published rise time tRt timed FROM THE FLASH and therefore included the 50-67 ms response time tR - a sensory and neural latency this model does not simulate.

parameters.name: target_duration_ms
parameters.source: Whole-event response duration rD of the EXPANSION response, 300-384 ms across body regions (Hadjisolomou SP et al. 2021, Front Physiol 12:675252, PMID 34220538 (read: full text via publisher)). The abstract's 217-384 ms range mixes this with the separate retraction-type response (n = 65 cells) and is not a comparison between phases.

parameters.name: target_asymmetry
parameters.source: Two measurements, both greater than 1, kept separate rather than averaged: 1.338 from contraction 5.90 +/- 3.50 vs expansion 4.41 +/- 1.91 frames at 20 fps (Renard MDM et al. 2026, eLife 110074, PMID 42418335 (read: full text via PMC); Euprymna berryi and Sepia officinalis), and 3.696 from Table 1 of Hadjisolomou SP et al. 2021, Front Physiol 12:675252, PMID 34220538 (read: full text via publisher) decomposed per region (Doryteuthis pealeii). They differ about 3x in magnitude and agree on sign.

model.parameter_note: `sourced` means the number appears in a paper we read, measured in the thing being modelled. A value measured in another tissue or another species is `assumed`, with the proxy named in `source`.

control.design: One parameter (sacculus shear modulus G) is fitted to ONE measured number (steady-state area ratio 2.55x). Rise time and the expansion:retraction asymmetry are then predictions with nothing further fitted. Dermal damping c is swept rather than fitted to expansion, and the c that would match the measured retraction is reported as a prediction about an unmeasured quantity.

settings.setting: longest drive that recovers the expansion magnitude

joint_feasibility.verdict: The model can reach EITHER measured asymmetry, so the earlier claim that a lumped elastic recoil is structurally incapable of retraction slower than expansion was WRONG - it was made from a sweep whose maximum sat at its own upper boundary. What is true is weaker and still a clear failure: no single setting satisfies more than one measured quantity. The damping that gives Renard's 1.34 costs a third of the expansion magnitude (2.06 -> 1.73 against a measured 2.55) and makes the already-failing rise time worse (215 -> 232 ms against a measured 67-83 ms). The damping that gives Hadjisolomou's 3.70 costs nearly half the expansion. Recovering the expansion magnitude on top needs a 2-second drive and a 1,674 ms rise, twenty times the measured expansion phase, against a whole response that completes in under 400 ms. The model is a one-constraint model being asked to meet three.

damping_sweep_reach.how_this_guard_was_broken: Its first version filtered with `if r["asymmetry..."]`, and NaN is TRUTHY in Python, so rows where the organ never returned were kept. The guard was then not merely wrong but INCAPABLE OF THE ALARMING ANSWER: every comparison against NaN is False, so `abs(amax - nan) < 1e-12` is False, which reads as 'the extremum is not at the boundary' - the reassuring verdict - whatever the data says. Worse, `max()` is order-dependent with a NaN present: max([1,2,nan,3]) is 3 while max([nan,1,2,3]) is nan, so whether the NaN even surfaced depended on row order. A guard that can only return 'fine' is not a guard. Fixed by filtering on math.isfinite and reporting how many points failed to return. The honest consequence: this field is now TRUE - the extremum IS at the boundary of the finite region - and the earlier `false` was never a measurement.
damping_sweep_reach.note: Whether the sweep's extremum sits at its own boundary is checked, because an extremum at the boundary is exactly the condition under which 'no value reaches X' cannot be claimed. It did, in the original -9..-2.5 range, and the claim made from it was wrong. It does again here, for a different reason: above c ~ 2 the organ no longer returns 90% of the way within the 6 s window, so the maximum reported is set by the window and NOT by the physics. The maximum is therefore not a quotable quantity. The CROSSING point is: it is interior to the finite region and robust, and it is the number this study relies on.

quotable.smallest_c_with_asymmetry_above_one: YES. It is interior to the finite region, and - the stronger evidence - it has not moved across every configuration in which it was observable: 0.1 under a 1.2 s integration window, 0.1 under a 6 s window, and 0.1 after the NaN-filter fix below. A quantity that is stable across three different runs of the machinery is a property of the model; one that moves with the machinery is a property of the run. (The ORIGINAL narrow sweep, c <= 3.2e-3, could not observe the crossing at all, which is the whole reason the claim made from it was wrong.)
quotable.asymmetry_max: NO. It is set by the integration window, not by the physics: above c ~ 2 the organ does not return 90% of the way inside the window, so the maximum is simply the last point that finished. It moved 4.5x - 2.946 to 13.27 - between two versions of the SAME correction purely because the window was lengthened. Do not put this number in prose.

damping_sweep_reach.why_the_maximum_moved_between_versions: An earlier version of this file reported a maximum of 2.946. It is now 13.27, and the reason is the simulation window, not a new result. The window was lengthened from 1.2 s to 6 s because the sacculus-elasticity sweep was returning NaN retraction times: at the asymmetry-fitted damping a soft sacculus does not return 90% of the way within 1.2 s, and reporting that as NaN hid a real outcome rather than recording it. With the longer window the high-damping retractions complete, so the measured ratios rise. The quantity the retraction actually rests on - the crossing point - is unchanged at c = 0.1 under both windows. This is exactly why the maximum is marked unquotable above: a number set by the integration window will move whenever the window does.

area_ratio.status: FITTED at steady state, then BROKEN by the damping fit
area_ratio.note: G is fitted so the STEADY-STATE area ratio is exactly 2.5506, which is why this is not a test. But the peak reached under a 250 ms drive at the damping that the asymmetry fit selects is far below it. The two fits are mutually inconsistent: fitting the damping to the measured asymmetry destroys the expansion ratio the stiffness was fitted to.

rise_time_ms.measured_quantity: expansion PHASE duration tRt - tR per body region: 67 ms (head/arms), 67 ms (fin), 83 ms (mantle)
rise_time_ms.note: Scored against the expansion PHASE, not against the published rise time tRt. tRt is timed from the flash and contains a 50-67 ms sensory and neural latency this model does not simulate, because the model's clock starts at drive onset. Against tRt the model is 1.4-1.8x too slow; against the phase it is 2.6-3.2x too slow. Correcting the comparator made the control arm fail by more.

retraction_vs_expansion_asymmetry.note: Two independent measurements in three species both put retraction SLOWER than expansion: 1.34 (Renard 2026, Euprymna berryi and Sepia officinalis) and 3.70 (Hadjisolomou 2021, Doryteuthis pealeii, decomposed per region from Table 1). The model gives a ratio below 1 and no damping in the sweep crosses 1.0, because a passive elastic recoil against a lumped dashpot cannot be slower than the powered contraction before it. This refutes the model's STRUCTURE, not its parameters: real chromatophore retraction is probably not a lumped elastic recoil. The damping was selected against the nearer of the two targets, which the model cannot reach, so that selection simply returns the largest ratio available and is not a fit.

hadjisolomou_table1_decomposed.source: Hadjisolomou SP et al. 2021, Front Physiol 12:675252, PMID 34220538, Table 1 (read: full text via PMC8250766). Species: Doryteuthis pealeii.
hadjisolomou_table1_decomposed.two_populations_warning: This paper's 'expansion' and 'retraction' are two RESPONSE TYPES over two different populations - 4,000 chromatophores in 166 trials that expanded to the flash, and 65 in 19 trials that retracted - not the two phases of one event. The abstract's '217 ms (fin, retraction) to 384 ms (heads/arms, expansion)' is a minimum and a maximum across those two populations AND across body regions, and reads as though expansion were the slower process. It is not a comparison. The 155.06% and 40.46% magnitudes are likewise peaks of two separate populations, and are NOT evidence that the organ fails to return to baseline: rD is defined as running to 'the return to the pre-flash state following the peak response'.

implied_dermal_damping_N_s_per_m.status: PREDICTION about a quantity nobody has measured

sweeps._note: `area_ratio` in these sweeps is the STEADY-STATE ratio from steady_area_ratio(), i.e. what the organ reaches if held open indefinitely. `control.comparisons.area_ratio` is a different quantity with the same name: the dynamic PEAK under a 250 ms drive, which is lower. At the fitted stiffness they are 2.55 and 1.73. Both are reported because the measured 2.5506 is what the stiffness was fitted to, while the peak is what the organ actually reaches in the time the real response takes. `retraction_time_90pct_ms` is NaN where the organ had not returned 90% of the way within the 6 s window - a real outcome at the asymmetry-fitted damping, not a numerical failure.

rows.note: N x a x sigma_max, proxy stress

rows.quantity: Stored elastic energy at full expansion

rows.note: elastic recoil is the return spring

limitations: This model is a one-constraint model being asked to meet three. It is fitted to the steady-state expansion ratio and then scored on expansion speed and on the expansion:retraction asymmetry, and no single setting meets more than one of them. Enough damping reaches either measured asymmetry, but at a cost of a third to a half of the expansion magnitude and a rise time that is already 2.6-3.2x too slow and gets slower. A next version needs a mechanism that slows retraction WITHOUT loading expansion - a viscoelastic sacculus whose stress relaxes during the hold, or an active brake - rather than more of the one knob this model has.

The two measured asymmetries differ by about 3x and are preserved separately rather than averaged. They are also different measurements in different animals: Renard tracks phases of individual slice events at 20 fps in Euprymna berryi and Sepia officinalis; the Hadjisolomou figure is decomposed by us from per-region summary statistics of a startle response in Doryteuthis pealeii, and that decomposition is ours, not the authors'.
The sacculus shear modulus has never been measured; it is the one fitted parameter, so the model cannot claim to predict the expansion ratio - it was told it.

Every muscle property is a PROXY from a different squid muscle (mantle circular or funnel retractor). No one has measured the contractile properties of a chromatophore radial muscle, so sigma_max, V_max and the activation kinetics are assumed.

The measured control target itself is a startle response, not a maximal contraction: Hadjisolomou et al. report what the organ did on a light flash, and state no maximum. The folklore figure of a ~7x diameter / ~50x area expansion traces, as far as we could follow it, to a secondary teaching page citing Cloney & Florey 1968; we could not read a primary source stating it, and so do not use it.

The geometry is axisymmetric, but the organ is not: Renard et al. 2026 show expansion is routinely anisotropic, with about four independently driven petal-shaped sectors per chromatophore. A single radius cannot express that, and the model therefore cannot represent the sub-chromatophore control that the real system has.
Radial muscles of neighbouring chromatophores make direct muscle-to-muscle contacts (Gauld et al. 2021), so an isolated single-organ model omits a real mechanical coupling.
The dermal damping is not measured anywhere; the value reported is what the model needs, not what the tissue has.

Holding cost is reported as mechanical stress and stored elastic energy only. We did not find a measured ATP cost for cephalopod obliquely striated muscle, so no metabolic number is given rather than a fabricated one.
